problem: The procedure never links β to the plant gain at the chosen ωc′. Step 6 then checks PM = 180° + ∠G(jωc′) + ∠C(jωc′) as if ωc′ were the gain crossover. Unless β is chosen so the lag attenuation cancels the plant gain there, |KG(jωc′)C(jωc′)| is not 1 and the number computed is not the phase margin.
fix: Add: choose β so that 20 log β = 20 log|KG(jωc′)| (with Kc = 1/β), then verify |KG(jωc′)C(jωc′)| = 1 before computing PM at ωc′.

problem: 'Increase β' works only with the Kc = 1/β option, where the extra attenuation lowers crossover. With the Kc = 1 option listed just above, raising β raises the low-frequency gain (and Kv) while the high-frequency loop gain stays the same, so crossover stays put or moves right and PM falls slightly. The advice is stated without that condition.
fix: Qualify it: with Kc = 1/β, increasing β lowers crossover and can raise PM up to a point; with Kc = 1, fix a small PM by lowering z or choosing a lower ωc′, and recheck the error specification because β changes Kv.
